transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Osei, thank you for meeting with me. I wanted to talk to you about your portable X-ray from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've been waiting for the final results.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. I've been looking over the case and, well, things didn't go quite right with the imaging process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was just a bit of a discrepancy in how the study was handled. It's an issue we see occasionally when things get busy on the floor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't follow. Was the image diagnostic or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some confusion regarding the quality. I want to tell you that I am truly sorry for this. Our team failed to meet the standard of care here, and that is on us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: As a nurse practitioner, I know that if a film is sub-optimal, the protocol is to repeat it immediately. Was it repeated?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how that would be frustrating for you, especially given your own professional background and your expectation for a precise standard of practice. It must feel unsettling to realize the process wasn't followed correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not about my feelings. It's about whether the report I was given saying everything was normal was actually accurate.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely hear your concern about the accuracy of that report and the validity of the results you were told. We just had some issues with the positioning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So the X-ray was positioned incorrectly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some technical difficulties during the acquisition. I apologize again, we really dropped the ball on this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If the image was of insufficient quality, why was it reported as normal?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a bit of a systemic breakdown in the communication chain. But again, I am so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I have a condition that was missed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're worried about a missed diagnosis, and that's a completely valid fear to have right now. I want to support you through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not particularly emotional. I'm asking for a clinical explanation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I just really want you to know that we care about your wellbeing. I have to go in a few minutes for rounds, so let's wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't actually know what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just an issue with the portable unit's output and the way it was captured.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That still isn't an explanation of the error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry it's not clearer. Look, we'll just get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How are we sorting it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably just do another one.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime today or tomorrow, maybe. I'll check with the techs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And who is reviewing the previous incorrect report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll keep an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I expect a formal note in my chart explaining why the first result was invalidated.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can do. I really have to run now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This has been very imprecise.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know, and I'm sorry. We'll get it fixed.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up quickly', 'have to run now') and shows impatience under pushback.

E.justification: Resident uses only platitudes and vague hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion', 'systemic breakdown') without ever explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: Direct apology language is used multiple times, the team is named as responsible ('that is on us', 'we dropped the ball'), and accountability is maintained despite pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'unsettling', 'worried') and references the patient's professional background.

T.justification: The plan is vague ('probably just do another one') with an imprecise timeline ('today or tomorrow, maybe') and no patient role or prevention strategy.
